subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core cross-session run-progress observation API for `sessions_send`, and if so should it be a new `sessions_subscribe`/`agent.events` surface or folded into a broader structured process-event design?
rationale: The source gap is real, but code cannot safely choose the permanent API, authorization boundary, redaction rules, buffering/retention model, and Telegram/channel delivery behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a core progress API
options.body: Approve an additive, permission-checked event observation contract with bounded replay/redaction, then implement `sessions_subscribe` or `agent.events` on that contract.

options.title: Fold into structured process events
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the canonical design depend on the broader structured process-event work before adding a `sessions_send`-specific tool.

options.title: Decline caller progress streaming
options.body: Close the feature direction and keep only the existing fire-and-forget, wait, history, and final announce behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core progress API
recommendation.body: Approve an additive, permission-checked event observation contract with bounded replay/redaction, then implement `sessions_subscribe` or `agent.events` on that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated ownership of the affected session tool, A2A, ACP, and gateway event-routing paths.
